 By Tom Kao November 13, 2026 Lee Se-young is taking on one of her most talked-about roles yet in "The Remarried Empress." Starring alongside Shin Min-a, Ju Ji-hoon and Lee Jong-suk, the actress plays Rashta, a runaway slave who catches Emperor Sovieshu's attention and becomes his mistress, putting his marriage to Empress Navier at risk. While her portrayal of the seemingly innocent yet ambitious character has been getting plenty of attention, Lee is no newcomer to the screen. From her unusual childhood debut to her surprising off-screen personality, here are five things worth knowing about the South Korean actress 
 She became a child actress for an unusual reason
 Photo: Instagram @seyoung_10
 Lee Se-young's acting career actually began for a rather unexpected reason. During an appearance on You Quiz on the Block , the actress revealed that her mother feared child abductions and thought having a familiar face on television might help keep her safe. Lee eventually made her acting debut in 1996, at just four years old, before gaining wider recognition for playing the young Choi Geum-young in Dae Jang Geum (2003), the hugely popular historical drama that became a hit across Asia.
 She successfully made the transition from child star to leading actress
 Photo: Instagram @seyoung_10
 Growing up in front of the cameras isn't always easy, and Lee Se-young faced her share of challenges along the way. Despite finding success as a child actress, she later went through a period when acting opportunities were harder to come by. But rather than giving up, she continued building her career through more mature roles. A major turning point came with the 2016 family drama The Gentlemen of Wolgyesu Tailor Shop , which earned her the Best New Actress award at the 2017 Baeksang Arts Awards and helped her move beyond her child-star image.

 She has earned a reputation as a historical drama queen
 Photo: MBC
 If Lee Se-young looks right at home in royal settings, there's a good reason. Over the years, she's appeared in several historical dramas, including The Crowned Clown (2019) and The Story of Park's Marriage Contract (2023). But perhaps her most memorable performance in the genre came with The Red Sleeve (2021), where she starred opposite 2PM's Lee Junho as court lady Seong Deok-im. The romantic historical drama became a huge hit, with their on-screen chemistry winning over viewers and earning Lee the Top Excellence Award at the 2021 MBC Drama Awards.
 She learned Japanese for What Comes After Love 
 Photo: Coupang Play
 Lee Se-young isn't afraid to step outside her comfort zone when it comes to acting. For the 2024 cross-cultural romance What Comes After Love , in which she starred opposite Japanese actor Sakaguchi Kentaro, she had to deliver more than 80 per cent of her dialogue in Japanese despite never having spoken the language before. In an interview, she admitted that learning unfamiliar vocabulary was challenging, especially when trying to react naturally to her co-stars. Still, she embraced the challenge and said the experience gave her the confidence to take on more roles in other languages.
 She has a surprisingly playful personality off-screen
 Photo: Instagram @seyoung_10
 While Lee Se-young often plays elegant and composed characters on screen, she's got a more playful side in real life. For one, she's reportedly a big fan of rock music, with bands such as AC/DC, Nirvana and X Japan among her favourites. She's also known for being thoughtful towards those around her. Her The Crowned Clown co-star Yeo Jin-goo once revealed that she took photos of crew members and wrote down their names so she could remember everyone on set. It's a small but rather sweet gesture that says a lot about her personality.
